title: Waterfall GPU Capacity & Token Price Elasticity - working sheet
summary: Working sheet exploring a waterfall-style regional capacity allocation model combined with token-price elasticity curves. Purpose: estimate $/1M token across regions under reserve/spot mixes and burst policies and derive recommended reserve commits by region for next 12 months.
model_overview: We model fleet capacity as a waterfall: first satisfy baseline reserved SLAs (dedicated), then fill predictable queued load with reserved burst buffer, then use spot/ondemand for transient bursts. Token unit-econ derived by mapping GPU-hour cost to tokens processed per GPU-hour using workload mix (chat vs completion) and KV-cache hit assumptions. We overlay token-price elasticity: higher per-token price reduces request rate and increases average prompt length (observed in A/B), we model +/-15% demand elasticity scenarios.
assumptions: GPU cost input is net hourly effective cost after discounts and overhead (power, infra ops). We use region-specific blended rates.
Tokens per GPU-hour baseline: 120M tokens for 40B LM inference (mix of 512/2048 seq); for chat-heavy workloads use 85M tokens/GPU-hour.
KV cache hit reduces effective token generation by 30% for cached prefixes; baseline cache-hit=20%.
Reserved commit discount vs on-demand: 40% for reserved, spot discounts vary by region (50-70% depending on market).
Target utilization bands: baseline reserved pool util=70%, burst buffer =50% of reserved, spot pool utilization=55%.
scenario_outputs: Base case (no elasticity): global $/1M tokens = weighted avg 0.0185 USD, GPU-burn 45k GPU-hours/month, runway 11 months at current credits
Aggressive burst (peak x1.6): $/1M tokens increases to 0.022 USD; spot usage jumps to 48% of tokens; tail latency risk increases
Reserve-heavy (commit +20%): blended $/1M tokens improves to 0.016 USD; utilization of reserved rises to 78%; burst fallback reduced
Elasticity downside (-15% demand): effective $/1M tokens falls to 0.017 USD due to lower absolute throughput but fixed infra costs persist
unit_econ_table: eu-west|A100-80GB|3.80|115000000|0.0330|higher infra tax, lower tokens/GPU-hour due to regional latency configs
asia-south|V100-32GB|2.10|90000000|0.0233|cheaper GPU-hour but lower tokens/GPU-hour for same model, consider quantization
capacity_waterfall_steps: 1) Baseline reserved pool: size to cover 50th percentile sustained QPS at 99ms P95 target
2) Reserved burst buffer: additional reserved capacity activated via autoscaler policies for predictable daily peaks
3) Spot/ondemand pool: used for unpredictable spikes and background batch workloads
4) Fallback routing: lower-capacity model variants and regional failover when both reserved and spot exhausted
5) Credit/pricing throttle: apply dynamic per-tenant rate limits when unit-econ exceeds threshold
sensitivity_analysis_notes: Token yield sensitivity: +/-10% tokens/GPU-hour changes $/1M by ~10-12%
Spot discount sensitivity: moving spot discounts from 60% to 50% (~10pp) increases blended $/1M by ~6-7%
Cache-hit improvements: +10pp cache-hit reduces effective GPU burn ~8-10% and lowers $/1M proportionally
Regional migration: moving 15% of asia-south load to us-west reduces global $/1M by ~1.2% but increases latency for APAC users
recommended_next_steps: Run a week-long synthetic load test with production prompt mix to validate tokens/GPU-hour estimates (INF-4321)
Simulate commit scenarios in the cost model for 12/24 month reserve right-sizing and evaluate cashflow impacts
Prototype autoscaler policy that prioritizes reserved-burst activation over spot scaling for controlled tail-latency
Add model-variant cost bucket in telemetry to attribute $/1M by model and prompt-length distribution
footprint_plan: Short-term: add 20% reserved capacity in eu-west to reduce on-demand exposure for enterprise customers. Mid-term: shift non-latency-sensitive batch workloads from us-west reserved to asia-south spot to arbitrage cost. Long-term: evaluate colocated cold-pool in central-region for preemptible batch with specialized quantized runtimes.
